clue.text: Crank who did badly in Lent, for example

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the word before it come out jumbled
the jumbled word is placed inside the fasting season that follows

blocks.note: the three letters of did, rearranged
Lent is a period of fasting, an example of a fast

explanation.surface: An eccentric who made a poor job of keeping Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' looks like a verb or a machine part, but here it is a person with an obsessive hobby horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist follows passing enthusiasms obsessively, which is one sense of the informal noun crank.

blocks.note: first meaning: wearing or lined with a fleece
second meaning: swindled, charged far too much

explanation.surface: Someone well wrapped up, but at a steep price.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the first sense is playful: dressed in a fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fleeced is slang for being overcharged or cheated, and literally to wear a woolly coat.

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
ounces are units of weight

explanation.surface: Someone rails against research into weights.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' lets the first piece sit above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, which is what inveighing against something means.

clue.text: Disinclined to act in plainer terms

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters across the next two words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Reluctant to take action, put more simply.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something sluggish or inactive, lacking any will or power to move.

clue.text: Two thirds of the deliveries completed?

definitions.text: Two thirds of the deliveries completed?

blocks.clueFragment: Two thirds of the deliveries completed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a courier or postman is most of the way through the round
setter's reading: balls bowled in cricket; an over has six, so with two thirds bowled a third of the over remains

explanation.surface: A delivery round that is mostly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, each called a delivery; the question mark flags the switch from post to bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: With four of an over's six balls bowled, a pair of balls remain for the bowler before the over ends.

blocks.note: first meaning, split as two words: gets on to, as onto a bus or ship
second meaning: a spouse's son from an earlier marriage

explanation.surface: Someone lodges with a member of their family.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as STEPS ON, the answer means boards; read whole, it is a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a family member by marriage, while stepping on a vessel or vehicle is boarding it.

blocks.note: south, a point of the compass
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A tip found on a bird's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the compass point above the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship, so the back of a vessel.

clue.text: Site meant originally for a small bar

indicators.note: taken as 'in an original way', the words are set out in a fresh, novel order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A location that was first intended for a little pub.
explanation.walkthrough: An estaminet is a small French café selling drinks, familiar to British soldiers in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word names a modest café-bar, the kind of small drinking place the clue describes.

indicators.note: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so the word it is joined to is set out wrongly

blocks.note: the five letters after the prefix, rearranged

explanation.surface: A backer's lack of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word mistrust splits into a prefix meaning wrongly and the word to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a brace or bar that holds up part of a structure, so a physical supporter.

clue.text: Out of the running at present in this location

blocks.note: now means at the present time
here means at this place

explanation.surface: A runner currently trailing far behind in this race.
explanation.walkthrough: A competitor finishing nowhere is unplaced, with no chance of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing nowhere in a race means being unplaced, wholly out of contention for a prize.

clue.text: Point in lake that might prove richly rewarding

indicators.note: the compass point sits inside the name of the lake

blocks.note: north, a point of the compass
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A spot on a lake that could turn out to pay handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the British machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers each month, so it may make a bondholder rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The random-number machine selects prize-winning Premium Bonds, so its choice can bring a large cash payout.

clue.text: Defeat on the cricket field, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to topple, as a government or ruler
second meaning: a fielder's throw that runs past the stumps, letting the batters take extra runs

explanation.surface: A loss suffered during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an overthrow is a return throw that misses the wicket and lets the batting side run again.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a regime is to bring about its defeat, and cricket uses the same word for a wayward return throw.

clue.text: TV programme anxiously watched at Cape Canaveral, presumably

definitions.text: anxiously watched at Cape Canaveral, presumably

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-running British teatime quiz of words and numbers

blocks.clueFragment: anxiously watched at Cape Canaveral, presumably
blocks.note: second meaning: the seconds ticked off before a rocket launch

explanation.surface: A television show nervously followed by staff at the Florida space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a Channel 4 quiz show in Britain; Cape Canaveral is where NASA launches rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Launch controllers track the descending sequence of seconds to lift-off, which shares its name with the British quiz show.

blocks.note: the German word for with
Royal Engineers, standard abbreviation for a soldier

explanation.surface: A hat linked with a soldier from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by bishops, a piece of ceremonial headwear.

blocks.note: first meaning: dodges, as a question or a blow
second meaning: trousers made of duck, a heavy cotton or linen fabric

explanation.surface: Someone steers clear of rough clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a strong canvas-like cloth, and trousers made of it were called ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging something is ducking it, and the plural also names trousers sewn from a tough canvas-like fabric.

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: Having a pint alongside a football follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is someone who backs a team or performer, which is what a supporter does.

blocks.note: first meaning: a military push forward, as a noun
second meaning: rude or upsetting, as an adjective

explanation.surface: An assault that upsets people.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military campaign of aggression, and offensive behaviour is insulting or unpleasant.

clue.text: Get rid of Jeremy's hearthside implements?

blocks.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
Jeremy Irons, the English actor

explanation.surface: Throwing out a man's fireside tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the reading of Jeremy's as Jeremy is: the actor's surname follows the sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire irons are the poker, tongs and shovel kept beside an open fireplace for tending the fire.

clue.text: Having the principal role at the front

blocks.note: first meaning: starring in a play or film
second meaning: ahead of the rest in a race

explanation.surface: Starring and also out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the starring part in a production, or being ahead in a contest, are both described by this phrase.

blocks.note: surface reading: the newspaper mentioned must be thrown out
setter's reading: spoken in slangy style, 'dis a paper' is what is heard, and a thing that has to go must vanish

explanation.surface: The newspaper just mentioned must be got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken carelessly, the answer sounds like 'dis a paper', and to go in the sense of vanish is its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out of sight or cease to exist is to vanish, which is the sense the question mark points to.

blocks.note: first meaning: settled, made up one's mind
second meaning: definite, unmistakable

explanation.surface: Determined to stand one's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled question has been decided, and a decided opinion is clear-cut and unwavering.

clue.text: Entire amount put by child on a plate

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
the L-plate shown by a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: The whole sum a youngster places on a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display a plate bearing a red L.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum reached when everything is added together, the whole figure.

clue.text: Armed Indian tribesmen getting lark to fly round tree

indicators.note: the letters scatter as if taking to the air, landing in a new order
the jumbled bird's letters go around the tree

blocks.note: the letters of lark, rearranged
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Armed tribesmen send a songbird soaring around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A lashkar is a body of armed tribal fighters in Afghanistan and the old North-West Frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urdu and Pashto word names a tribal militia or armed band of fighters.

indicators.note: something internal is inside, so the measure goes within the firm's abbreviation

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A company's own measuring device.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family, played seated.

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: the lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A creature rumoured to be well connected.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are ties or joins between things, so another word for connections.

blocks.note: first meaning: weak-willed, lacking resolve
second meaning: literally having no backbone

explanation.surface: A wavering creature without a backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a backbone describes both a creature without vertebrae and a person who cannot make firm decisions.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only one possible arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the letters of lido, rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimming pool in the south of the country that is doing well financially.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid business is sound and reliable, in good financial health.

clue.text: Follow sun moving from east to east?

indicators.note: moving the letters around puts them in a new order

blocks.note: E for east, at the start
the letters of sun, rearranged
E for east again, at the finish

explanation.surface: Track the sun as it travels around the sky, from east back to east.
explanation.walkthrough: Both easts give E, placed either side of the jumbled sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards or result, which is to follow in time.

blocks.note: Robert Donat, British film star of the 1930s, known for The 39 Steps
a greeting with its first letter dropped, the same casual style as 'owdo

explanation.surface: A painter greets a veteran performer in broad northern dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owdo is a dropped-aitch greeting; its equivalent here is 'ELLO, likewise without its H. The greeting is attached to the actor, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the Florentine Renaissance sculptor, so an artist in the broad sense.

indicators.note: declared means said out loud, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

blocks.note: a stake is a financial interest or share in something

explanation.surface: Someone openly admits a financial interest in the meat trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak is a thick slice of beef cut for grilling or frying, a common kind of meat.

indicators.note: changing the word means its letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of side, rearranged
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone requested that a team switch its kit colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked in the sense of wished for or wanted: what was asked for is what was desired.

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a lender supplies money, such as a bank

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare scholar's backup provider of funding.
explanation.walkthrough: Slender is the foolish suitor of Anne Page in The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Slender is a comic character in one of the Bard's plays, so he is a Shakespearean figure.
